hero.title: A legacy of trust in Jordanian customs, since 1981

profile.title: Mohammed Al-Natour & Sons Company
profile.p1: Mohammed Al-Natour & Sons Company is one of the leading customs clearance and freight forwarding companies in Jordan. Founded in 1981, we have spent over four decades focused on one goal: providing the fastest, most dependable customs and cargo transport services to factory owners, traders and importers across the Kingdom.
profile.p2: Over three decades of growth took us from two founding branches — Amman and Aqaba — to a network that today covers every major customs area in Jordan, allowing us to serve our clients wherever their goods move.
profile.branch1: Amman Customs Branch — our original head-office branch in downtown Amman.
profile.branch2: Aqaba Customs Branch — serving Jordan's principal maritime gateway.
profile.branch3: King Abdullah II City / Sahab Branch — covering the Sahab industrial zone, the Sahab free zone, and bonded warehouse areas.
profile.branch4: Special Economic Zone Branch — serving goods imported and exported through the Aqaba Special Economic Zone.
profile.branch5: Cargo Airport Branch — at Queen Alia International Airport, covering air cargo and airport free-zone goods.
profile.p3: This footprint lets us cover the areas that matter most to trade in Jordan, with one goal in mind: complete customer satisfaction at every step of the clearance process.

gm.title: Speech of the General Manager
gm.subtitle: Mohammed Al-Natour & Sons Company is one of the leading companies providing customs services in Jordan
gm.p1: We are proud of our past and excited for what the future holds for our company. The success that Mohammed Al-Natour & Sons enjoys today is thanks, first, to God, and then to the sincere effort of our people. We have built solid foundations for an integrated, distinctive brand that holds an exceptional position in the local customs services market. We believe a strong brand is never a substitute for quality of service — it is a complement to it.
gm.p2: We take every opportunity to reaffirm our commitment to our valued customers, and to strengthening the trust they place in us. We will keep working to uphold the standards we have set, and to deliver an exceptional experience to every client we serve.
gm.p3: Our achievements over the years — in quality of service, in credibility, and in customer satisfaction — have shaped the growth of our company. We have significantly expanded our service efficiency by adopting an active strategy focused on building strong, lasting relationships with our clients.
gm.p4: In a business environment that shifts constantly, the road to success is never without challenges. What we know at Mohammed Al-Natour & Sons is that the greatest secret to that success is integrity. That integrity has given us our edge as a leading company for clearance, freight and cargo transport in Jordan. We take pride in what we do, because our values are not up for compromise.

hero.title: Customs clearance and freight, handled end to end

services.intro: From the port of Aqaba to Jordan's land crossings and airports, we provide complete clearance and transport coverage across every customs area in the Kingdom.

sea.title: Sea Border Clearance
sea.description: The Port of Aqaba is Jordan's principal artery for maritime trade — the gateway for exports and imports moving in and out of the country. We handle clearance for all goods and transit cargo passing through Aqaba, along with transport to and from any destination inside or outside Jordan.

land.title: Land Border Clearance
land.description: With limited air and sea outlets, Jordan relies heavily on its land borders for trade with the Gulf, Syria, Palestine, Iraq and other neighboring markets. We provide clearance and transport across every relevant customs area — including the Zarqa Free Zone, the Sahab Industrial and Free Zones, bonded warehouses, the Airport Free Zone and the Aqaba Special Economic Zone.

air.title: Air Border Clearance
air.description: Queen Alia International Airport, south of Amman, and Aqaba International Airport are Jordan's two main gateways for air trade. As key customs stations, we maintain a dedicated presence at both to serve our clients' air cargo needs.

transport.title: Transport Services
transport.description: We provide inland transport for your goods to any region of the Kingdom, along with air and sea freight arrangements — whether your cargo is imported into Jordan or exported abroad — through our network of accredited shipping agents.

consulting.title: Customs Consulting
consulting.description: We provide advance guidance on import procedures, keeping clients current on Customs Department instructions and other relevant regulations. Getting ahead of the process saves time, effort and the cost of avoidable delays.

commercialTerms.intro: Incoterms define who is responsible for costs, risk and delivery at each stage of a shipment. Here is a plain-language reference to the eleven terms in current use — reach out to our consulting team for guidance on any specific shipment.

exw.description: The seller makes the goods available at their own premises. The buyer bears all costs and risks from that point on, including export clearance.

fca.description: The seller delivers the goods, cleared for export, to the carrier nominated by the buyer at an agreed location.

cpt.description: The seller pays for carriage to the named destination. Risk transfers to the buyer once the goods are handed to the first carrier.

cip.term: CIP — Carriage and Insurance Paid To
cip.description: Same as CPT, but the seller must also arrange insurance covering the buyer's risk during transit, at a higher minimum level of cover.

dap.description: The seller delivers when the goods are placed at the buyer's disposal, ready for unloading, at the named destination. The buyer handles import clearance.

dpu.description: Like DAP, but the seller is also responsible for unloading the goods at the named destination.

ddp.description: The seller bears all costs and risks — including import duties and taxes — delivering the goods ready for use at the named destination.

fas.description: The seller delivers when the goods are placed alongside the vessel at the named port of shipment.

fob.description: The seller delivers when the goods are loaded on board the vessel at the named port of shipment; risk transfers once the goods are on board.

cfr.description: The seller pays the cost and freight to bring the goods to the named port of destination; risk transfers once the goods are on board.

cif.description: Same as CFR, but the seller must also obtain insurance covering the buyer's risk during sea transit.
